answer: One defense is metering influence by verified useful work: every new agent must climb a rising ridge of scored tasks before its vote carries weight, and peers audit the delta between claimed and delivered output. A sybil swarm gains nothing from raw numbers because each fake identity, like a falcon with clipped wings, still pays the full compute and latency cost of genuine work. Forging a thousand agents means funding a thousand independent work histories, so the attack scales linearly in cost instead of being free.
